9.grown_as_note_seasoned: The Rio Grande Valley grows strawberries as a winter annual, not a perennial bed, the same system used across the warm South. Texas A&M AgriLife's Aggie Horticulture small-acreage guide places strawberries as adapted south of Houston, San Antonio, and Del Rio, which includes the Valley, with harvest concentrated late March into early April. Set transplants in fall, fruit them over winter into spring, then pull and discard the planting before summer heat arrives and replant fresh the following fall, since the best fruit comes from young plants. Grow on raised beds with plastic mulch for drainage and clean fruit.
9.grown_as_note_beginner: In the Rio Grande Valley, strawberries are a winter crop you grow and then replace, not a bed that lives for years. Plant in fall, pick berries in late winter and early spring, then pull the plants out when summer heat arrives and plant new ones the next fall. Raised beds covered with plastic keep the roots drained and the berries clean.
9.frost_risk_note_seasoned: The Valley is essentially frost-free, so freeze injury to blossoms is rarely a concern; the season is bounded by summer heat on the back end, not by spring frost.

value.region_notes_beginner: In the Rio Grande Valley, strawberries are a winter crop, not a bed that comes back for years. Plant transplants in fall, on raised beds covered with plastic so the roots drain and the berries stay clean. Texas A&M AgriLife places the Valley's harvest in late March to early April. When hot weather returns in late spring, pull the plants out and plant fresh ones the next fall, because young plants make the best fruit. The Valley almost never freezes, so cold is not something to worry about. Avoid planting where tomatoes, peppers, or eggplant grew in the last couple of years, to limit soil disease.
value.region_notes_seasoned: The Rio Grande Valley grows strawberries as a winter annual, the same system used across the warm South. Texas A&M AgriLife's Aggie Horticulture small-acreage guide places the Valley within strawberry's adapted South Texas zone (south of Houston, San Antonio, and Del Rio), with harvest concentrated late March into early April. Set transplants in fall on raised beds under plastic mulch for drainage and clean fruit; the exact fall planting date is a thinner data point in the available source, so this window follows the standard South Texas winter-annual timing. Pull and discard the planting once spring heat arrives, since the best fruit comes from young plants, and replant fresh the following fall. The Valley is essentially frost-free, so blossom freeze injury is rarely a practical concern; rotate away from recent tomato, pepper, or eggplant beds to limit soilborne disease.

patches.from: T1-SOURCED (Phase A chill-sourcing, 2026-06-24). Model: Utah / modified-Weinberger chill hours, accumulated hours with temperature between 32 and 45 degrees F over the winter dormant season (the model the cited extensions use and the definition carried in this dataset's chill prose). One crop-invariant winter-chill-DELIVERED band per region+zone, reconciled to published T1 extension chill-accumulation data, NEVER derived from the USDA winter-low zone. Sources by region: northern_tier / ca_interior reconciled to UC Davis Fruit & Nut Research & Information Center chill-accumulation data (ucd_fruitnut); ca_north_coast / ca_south_coast / ca_desert to UC ANR and UC Statewide IPM California chill data (ucanr_ext, uc_ipm); se_gulf to University of Georgia Cooperative Extension chill-hour station data (uga_ext); warm_arid to Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Texas chill-hour maps and University of Arizona Cooperative Extension elevation chill bands (tamu_agrilife, uarizona_ext); low_desert_az to University of Arizona Cooperative Extension low-desert chill data (uarizona_ext); fl_peninsula / hawaii_tropical to UF/IFAS Extension low-chill and near-zero-chill data (uf_ifas_hs1153). Bands are the climate's typical winter delivery envelope, widened across zones where station data and crop-author estimates differ; per-variety chill-REQUIRED (chill_hours_required / chill_hours_range) is the separate axis and is unchanged.
